recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Owls, Meditation, and Daily Practice", "body": "Gordan Hamil described a daily meditation practice kept under an owl tree, where he said he let the owls come close without forcing the connection until they allowed him into their life. He named the matriarch Gwen and a second pair of owls that followed him on nightly desert walks. Gordan explained memento mori as accepting that we are mortal and the idea of surrender. Later he showed video of the nest and said he planned a game camera live feed and a falconer course at the Sonoran Desert Museum."}, {"title": "Mutants and Shamanic Initiation", "body": "Chance argued that the shamanic healing crisis, in which a person either dies or becomes magic, matched the emergence of the mutant gene in the X-Men. Gordan said an online stranger once told him that owls symbolize rebirth and that he might be passing through a shamanic initiation, which showed him his bond with the owls ran deeper than observation. The conversation then turned to the hero's journey, with Gordan saying comics and myth keep telling listeners that they are the superhero and can do the work themselves."}, {"title": "Nature, Breath, and the Template of Wholeness", "body": "Chance defined nature as life force energy, linking it to Wilhelm Reich's ether and Walter Russell's single column of consciousness, God and spirit. He argued that aligning with breath and nature meant embodying the template of wholeness, so the body healed itself, and that quieting the monkey mind helped a person get out of the way. Chance said fifteen minutes was his sweet spot for feeling the parasympathetic nervous system activate, and he cautioned against promising listeners particular visions."}, {"title": "Comics as Participatory Alchemy", "body": "Gordan argued that comics pulled readers into the story as participants, while film and TV left them passive. Gabe said the word comic implied a co-made experience and called nostalgia a powerful alchemical ingredient that kept people in a state of perpetual youth. Johnny Larson said Hollywood made comic movies huge to turn grown men into children. Chance described the space between frames as a liminal gap where each reader made a unique movie in the mind, and the hosts later promoted their Marvelous Demystifiers series, which decodes Marvel films and began with Eternals."}, {"title": "Shape Shifting, Animals, and Synchronicity", "body": "One of the hosts read from the book Shaman Healer Sage about shamans projecting consciousness into animals. Gordan said he had tried it in lucid dream work, first as a coyote and then as a hawk. A host relayed the book's claim that the key was seeing oneself as no more or less important than anything else, and a voice on the call contrasted this with skinwalkers, described as dark control of an animal. Later a host described a shared meditation with Gordan in which both saw the same butterfly, which the host took as a sign of being on the right path."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Fellow Weaving Spider Gordy Hamil joins Vibe Rant to help us usher in the era of Mutants, share massive healing experiences gained from his meditation practice, and give us an update on the parliament of owls that have accepted him as their human ambassador.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I see your journey as shamanic because in my shamanism, there's a really consistent aspect to it where people go through a major healing crisis, where they're either going to die or they're going to become magic. And to me, that's kind of like the emergence of the mutant gene in the X-Men.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And so as I'm meditating and kind of praying and really embracing that it's possible to get close to these owls in an authentic relationship, and just kind of letting it happen instead of forcing myself on them, I would just go out and do it every day. And they allowed me into their life.", "author": "Gordan Hamil", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "I think people would benefit from 20, 15, even 10 minutes a day. For me, 15 minutes is like the sweet spot where I feel the parasympathetic nervous system activate. And like, I feel my heart rate change. I feel myself settle into it. And it's almost like that's the point where you're just beginning to actually meditate.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And you kind of have to surrender something. It was like two years of my meditation practice where almost every time after like 10 minutes into it, my brain had just started being like, oh shit, man, you're going to die, man. Now that's not even a thing.", "author": "Gordan Hamil", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So when you're getting in tune or alignment with spirit or your breath in nature, you are basically inhaling and embodying the template of wholeness that created you in the first place. And that's how your body heals itself. Nothing heals your body for it. It does it itself. And it uses that Chi or that Prana to do it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And comics do not need to be even called comics. We could call it graphic novels or something else. And they don't necessarily need to be tied to these licensed characters. But that seems to be the only way that the industry makes the money to continue, by rehashing and recycling the same characters ad nauseam.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But there is also a visual reference that adds to that story. Whereas with TV and movies, it's just telling you, you just have to be a passive participant. It just tells you what you're getting. And you want to be participatory in a book, in a comic, you're part of the story. So I think that's why the medium is important.", "author": "Gordan Hamil", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "We're making it together. It's that creative experience of the book. The original experience was cooperative. And, you know, they were able to imply things. And you met them halfway. So the comics were co-made.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I do feel like Hollywood and, like, making all these comic movies and stuff huge is just to make grown men into like little children. I love all this stuff, and I love connecting with my childhood on some level. But, dude, I know some people that, like, this is their religion. They like fight you if you tell them the Spider-Man movie sucked.", "author": "Johnny Larson", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "To be attached to these ideas that bring us back to our childhood, they have that nostalgia, which is one of the most powerful alchemical ingredients there is, that they keep us in a state of childhood and perpetual youth, which is, you know, a fantasy.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Film is almost like switching you into this hypnotic mode, where you're just programmed to receive because you don't need to fill any gaps yourself with a novel. You're making the mental movie in your head with comic books. You have this space, the liminal space between the frames. And in that space, you are creating a unique experience of the story that's different from everyone else.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm like, okay, I'm going to see if I can get in a coyote and see what the desert's like from a coyote's point of view. And you're feeling it, you're experiencing exactly as coyote. And once you realize you're in coyote, you're like, I am coyote. And you're like, oh my God, I'm part of everything.", "author": "Gordan Hamil", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So he can keep an eye on the other side of the desert while I'm keeping an eye on this side of the desert. They treat me kind of like one of them. And it's an amazing, amazing thing. And I will continue to document this as long as it goes on.", "author": "Gordan Hamil", "portrait": ""}]
fields.Title: Owls, Mutants & Meditation with Gordy Hamil
